topic: Sakura's fake confession in chapter 469 was a cover for the plan to kill Sasuke, and Naruto saw through the lie without knowing why
title: Sakura's Lie To Naruto Wasn't About Love
description: Sakura told Naruto she loved him in chapter 469, and Naruto knew it was a lie. Here is what she was really hiding and why it hurts more on a rewatch. Did Naruto fail her, or did she fail him?
comment: Was Sakura right to lie to Naruto in the Land of Iron, or should she have told him the truth? Pick a side.

lines.text: Sakura's lie to Naruto in the Land of Iron wasn't about love at all.

shot.search: Sakura Naruto Land of Iron confession
shot.fallback: pink haired kunoichi facing a blond ninja

lines.text: It was a cover story, and I think Naruto felt that instantly.

shot.fallback: blond ninja listening to a girl

lines.text: Chapter 469. Sakura says she loves Naruto and tells him to forget Sasuke.

shot.fallback: girl confessing to a blond boy

lines.text: But here is what she left out. Konoha had already decided to kill Sasuke.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja in a red cloud cloak

lines.text: She couldn't say that out loud, because it would break Naruto's promise to her.

shot.search: Naruto promise of a lifetime Sakura
shot.fallback: blond ninja giving a thumbs up

lines.text: So she tried to talk him into quitting, and Naruto stopped her mid sentence.

shot.search: Naruto stops Sakura lying to herself

lines.text: He told her she was lying to herself. Not lying to him. To herself.
People say he was stubborn. But look at what she did next.
She left Naruto behind and went to kill Sasuke herself, and her hand froze.
Naruto saw the one thing she couldn't hide, that she could never actually do it.
Her lie never fooled him, and that is why he kept the promise.
Sakura's lie to Naruto in the Land of Iron wasn't about love...
